78.h: 74 - Usayd ibn al-Ḥuḍayr ibn Simāk ibn ʿAtīk al-Anṣārī *
78.t:
ibn Nāfiʿ ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal. ⟦1:340⟧
The Imam (الإمام) Abū Yaḥyā - and it is said: Abū ʿAtīk - al-Anṣārī, al-Awsī, al-Ashhalī.
One of the twelve leaders on the night of al-ʿAqabah; he accepted Islam early.
He said: he did not witness Badr. His father was a noble, obeyed man, called: Ḥuḍayr of the Squadrons, and he was chief of the Aws on the day of Buʿāth (1) , and he was killed that day, six years before the year of the Hijrah. Usayd was counted among the wise nobles and the men of sound judgment.
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: The Prophet ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Zayd ibn Ḥārithah.
He has a narration of a few hadiths.
Narrating from him: عائشة، وكعب بن مالك، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، and he did not meet him.
al-Wāqidī mentioned: that he came to al-Jābiyah with ʿUmar, and was placed in charge of a quarter of the Anṣār, and that he was among those who accepted Islam at the hands of Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, he and Saʿd ibn Muʿādh (2) .
Abū Hurayrah said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What an excellent man is Abū Bakr, what an excellent man is ʿUmar, what an excellent man is Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr."
It was reported by: al-Tirmidhī (3) , and its chain of transmission (إسناده) is good.
It is narrated that Usayd was among the people with the finest voice in reciting the Qurʾān. ⟦1:341⟧
ابن إسحاق: عن يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله، عن عائشة، قالت:
Three of the Anṣār from Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal - no one was reckoned to rival them in excellence after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr, and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr - may Allah be pleased with them (1) -.
Ibn Isḥāq said: Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr was a leader who did not witness Badr, and his patronymic (الكنية) was: Abū Yaḥyā.
It is said: Usayd had a playful humour and a pleasant character.
روى حصين، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، عن أسيد بن حضير، who was given to joking:
That he was with the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ poked him with a stick he had with him, so he said: Let me retaliate.
He said: "Retaliate."
He said: You are wearing a shirt, and I am not wearing a shirt.
He said: So the Prophet ﷺ lifted up his shirt.
He said: Then he began kissing his side, and saying:
This is all I wanted, O Messenger of Allah (2) .
أبو صالح كاتب الليث: حدثنا يحيى بن عبد الله بن سالم، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال:
When Usayd ibn al-Ḥuḍayr died, and his creditors rose to claim their money, ʿUmar asked: in how many years would its fruit pay off what he owed of the debt?
It was said to him: in four years.
So he said to his creditors: What harm is it to you if it is not sold?
They said: Decide, for we only seek settlement within four years.
They agreed to that, so the property was left to them.
He said: He had not sold the date palms of Usayd for four years to ⟦1:342⟧ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, but rather he placed it in the hands of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān for the creditors (1) .
عبد الله بن عمر: عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال:
Usayd died and left a debt of four thousand upon himself, and his land yielded a thousand each year, so they wanted to sell it.
So ʿUmar sent to his creditors: Would you agree to receive a thousand each year?
They said: Yes (2) .
Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr said: Usayd died in the year 20, and ʿUmar carried him between the two poles, the two poles of the bier, until he set him down at al-Baqīʿ (3) , then prayed over him.
al-Wāqidī, Abū ʿUbayd, and a group dated his death to it.
He regretted having stayed behind from Badr, and said: I thought it was the caravan, and had I thought it was a military expedition I would not have stayed behind (4) .
He was wounded on the day of Uḥud (5) with seven wounds. ⟦1:343⟧

79.h: 75 - al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr ibn Ṭarīf al-Dawsī *
79.t:
A Companion of the Prophet ﷺ; he was an obeyed chief, one of the nobles of the Arabs.
Daws is a clan of al-Azd.
Al-Ṭufayl was nicknamed: Dhū al-Nūr (1) ; he accepted Islam before the Hijrah, in Mecca.
Hishām ibn al-Kalbī said: al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr ibn Ṭarīf was called Dhū al-Nūr; because he said:
O Messenger of Allah! Adultery has overcome Daws, so supplicate to Allah against them.
He said: "O Allah, guide Daws."
Then he said: O Messenger of Allah! Send me to them, and give me a sign.
So he said: "O Allah, give him light" ... , and he mentioned the hadith (2) .
In (the Military Campaigns of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī): حدثنا الكلبي، عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، عن الطفيل الدوسي (3) . ⟦1:344⟧
Ibn Isḥāq mentioned him, with: عن عثمان بن الحويرث، عن صالح بن كيسان, that al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr said:
I was a poet, a chief among my people, and I came to Mecca and went to the men of Quraysh, and they said: You are a poet and a chief, and we fear that this man will meet you and afflict you with some of his speech, for his speech is like magic, so beware lest he bring upon you and your people what he brought upon us, for he has split a man from his brother, a man from his wife, and a man from his son.
By Allah, they kept telling me about his affair and forbidding me to listen to him, until I said: By Allah, I will not enter the mosque except with my ears stopped.
He said: So I went to my ears and stuffed them with cotton (1) , then went out early to the mosque, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing in the mosque, so I stood near him, and Allah would not have it but that He make me hear some of his words.
So I said to myself: By Allah, this is truly helplessness, and I am a steady man, matters are not hidden from me, the good of them and the bad. By Allah, I will listen to him; if his affair is right guidance I will take from him, and if not I will avoid him.
So I pulled out the cotton, and I never heard speech finer than the speech he was uttering.
I said: Glory be to Allah! I have never heard a day like today any wording finer or more beautiful than it.
When he left I followed him, and entered his house with him, and said:
O Muḥammad! Your people came to me and said to me such and such, and I told him what they said, and Allah would not have it but that I hear from you what you say, and it has fallen into my heart that it is true, so present your religion to me.
So he presented Islam to me, and I accepted Islam, then I said:
I am returning to Daws, and I am obeyed among them, and I will call them to Islam, perhaps Allah will guide them, so supplicate to Allah to give me a sign.
He said: "O Allah, give him a sign that will help him."
So I set out until I came to the mountain pass of my people, and my father, a very old man, was there, and my wife and my children. When I climbed the pass, Allah placed between my eyes a light like a flame, which a person present could see in the darkness of the night, while I was descending from the pass.
I said: O Allah, not in my face, ⟦1:345⟧ for I fear they will think it is a mutilation because of my leaving their religion.
So it moved, and settled on the end of my whip, and I saw myself riding on my camel toward them, while it was on the end of my whip like a hanging lamp.
He said: My father came to me, and I said: Keep away from me, for I am not of you, and you are not of me.
He said: And why is that?
I said: I have accepted Islam, and followed the religion of Muḥammad.
He said: O my son! My religion is your religion, and likewise my mother; so the two accepted Islam.
Then I called Daws to Islam, but they refused me and were disobedient.
Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
Adultery and usury have overcome Daws, so supplicate against them.
He said: "O Allah, guide Daws."
Then I returned to them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ emigrated, and I stayed among them calling them to Islam, until those who responded among them responded, and Badr, Uḥud and the Trench passed me by.
Then I came with eighty or ninety households from Daws, and I was with the Prophet ﷺ until the conquest of Mecca.
I said: O Messenger of Allah! Send me to Dhū al-Kaffayn, the idol of ʿAmr ibn Ḥumamah, so that I may burn it.
He said: "Yes, go out to it."
So I went, and began kindling a fire upon it.
Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and stayed with him until he was taken, then I went out with the expedition against Musaylimah, with my son ʿAmr, until when I was on some part of the road, I saw a dream: I saw that my head was shaved, and a bird came out of my mouth, and a woman put me into her private part, and my son was seeking me eagerly, but he was kept from me.
I told my people about it, and they said: Good.
I said: As for me, I have interpreted it: as for the shaving of my head: it is its cutting off.
And the bird: it is my soul.
And the woman: the earth in which I will be buried; I was alarmed that I would be killed as a martyr.
And as for my son's seeking me: I only see that he will be excused in his seeking of martyrdom, and I do not see him reaching me on this journey of his.
He said: So al-Ṭufayl was killed on the day of al-Yamāmah, and his son was wounded, then was killed on the day of al-Yarmūk afterward (1) . ⟦1:346⟧
I say: His son ʿAmr has been counted among the Companions (الصحابي), and likewise his father should be counted among the Companions (الصحابي), for he accepted Islam according to what we have mentioned, but it has not reached us that he emigrated, nor that he saw the Prophet ﷺ.
